::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-small-biter"}
The small biter is the first and cheapest breed, raised from the wild stock and marked with green and yellow bands. A young culture's waves are mostly small biters. Any turret stops them, as long as it is fed.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-medium-biter"}
The medium biter is the small biter with armor added, bred once the culture's evolution has risen. A culture that has lost its clinic falls back to mediums and smalls. Keep your gun turrets well supplied, or add lasers.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-spore"}
The Spore spitter is the only breed that attacks fliers, with spores that burst where they land. Most waves bring a few. Combat robots and drones that fly over a wave die to them. Keep your robots out of a wave's path and leave it to the turrets.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-medium-spitter"}
The medium spitter stays behind the wall and lobs acid over it at whatever stands close behind. It is fragile, but it punishes turrets placed right against the wall. Give your turrets the reach to hit it beyond the wall.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-cinder"}
The burster is a small biter bred into a walking bomb. It cannot bite. It runs to a wall or turret, stops, swells and explodes, and if killed on the way it explodes where it falls. Shoot bursters while they run: once one has stopped to swell, it will go off.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-big-biter"}
The big biter is the bulk of a grown culture's waves. Big biters run past turrets they have no need to fight and go for the poles and inserters behind them. Protect your power and ammunition supply with a second line of turrets.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-stomper"}
The stomper is a pentapod brought from Gleba, tall enough to step over a wall. Bullets do little to it. It crosses your wall and goes for whatever the wave came for. Rocket troopers and battle tanks bring it down; keep rockets near the wall.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-behemoth-biter"}
The behemoth is the heaviest and most expensive breed. It arrives late and in small numbers, and it survives what kills the rest of the wave. Artillery, massed lasers and battle tanks deal with it. Keep your defenses deep.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-big-burster"}
The big burster is a behemoth bred around an explosive gland. It is sent at one of the turrets covering the wave's approach, and its blast damages every turret nearby. Killed early, only part of it goes off. Space your turrets apart.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-sweeper"}
The sweeper is bred to clear minefields. It walks into the mines and sets them off, tough enough to last the few seconds that takes. Waves whose route crosses mines send sweepers first. Cover your minefields with turrets.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-scout"}
The scout is a small, fast biter sent ahead of each wave to circle your defenses just outside turret range. It does not fight. A killed scout leaves a skull where it fell, and the next one circles wider. A scout at your wall means a wave is coming.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-carrier"}
The carrier is a glowing violet big biter that leads a group of stock to a wild nest field further out and starts a new culture there. It avoids fights and paths around cliffs and buildings. Kill it on the way and the new culture never starts.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-technician"}
Technicians are the only Synthexis staff on the ground: workers in sealed suits who carry feed between the biochambers. Without them the biochambers stop, and without the biochambers the incubators stop breeding. Shoot the technicians first.
:::
